Seminar Title:

Development of Efficient Multi-modal Fusion Techniques for Infrared and Visible Images

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

Electrical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Ankan Banerjee ( Rollno : 520ee1005)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

EE 401 (Smart Seminar Room)

Date and Time:

05 Aug 2026 2.00 PM

Contact:

Dipti Patra

Abstract:

Infrared&ndashvisible (IR&ndashVIS) image fusion is a key component of multimodal vision systems, enabling the integration of complementary thermal and visual information to improve perception under challenging imaging conditions. Despite extensive research, existing fusion approaches often rely on handcrafted rules, exhibit limited global context modeling, inadequately preserve spatial structure, and remain weakly aligned with downstream vision tasks. This thesis addresses the above limitations by proposing a systematic progression of fusion frameworks that advance image fusion of infrared and visible images from signal-level integration toward structured, expressive, and task-driven fusion. The study begins with an adaptive Empirical Wavelet Transform (EWT)-based fusion framework that offers interpretable multi-scale decomposition and effective preservation of thermal saliency and structural details. Building on this foundation, deep encoder&ndashdecoder architectures enhanced with attention mechanisms and transformer-based global modeling are developed to enable learnable multi-scale feature extraction and improved long-range dependency capture. To further enrich feature representations, a hybrid quantum&ndashclassical fusion framework is introduced, integrating variational quantum circuits as nonlinear feature transformers within the fusion pipeline. In parallel, a capsule-based fusion architecture is proposed to explicitly model spatial hierarchies and part&ndashwhole relationships, ensuring structurally consistent fusion through dynamic routing. Finally, the thesis advances toward machine-centric perception by introducing task-driven fusion strategies jointly optimized with downstream objectives such as object detection. The proposed methods are validated on benchmark datasets including TNO, RoadScene, LLVIP, and Harvard CT&ndashMRI, demonstrating consistent improvements in perceptual quality, structural and information preservation, and task-level performance.
